name: Tamale

seoDescription: Learn what the Tamale emoji 🫔 really means.

longForm.overview:
The 🫔 Tamale emoji was added in Unicode 13 (2020) and is drawn as a wrapped tamale in a green corn husk with the ends tied, often showing a small piece of filling visible at the top. The visual cue reads instantly as tamale-coded reference, Mexican default, or the visible 'wrapped meal' tag. By 2026 🫔 has become the go-to emoji for the tamale reaction, the visible wrapped-meal default, and the Mexican-food coded reaction in close-friends and family chats.

In modern chat 🫔 does very specific work. People send it as a literal tamale reference, as the visible 'wrapped meal' tag, or as the Mexican-food-coded default. The green corn husk wrap with tied ends is the visual cue that the read is tamale-coded. Writers should pick 🫔 when the read is tamale or visible 'Mexican food' energy, and avoid it when the read is burrito — 🌯 fits better there.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
🫔 lands on a friend's 'taco tuesday' message, in a work channel where someone is signaling Mexican-food energy, and in a family group where the sender is referencing a traditional meal. The green corn husk wrap with tied ends anchors the read.

In close-friends chats 🫔 reads as the universal tamale default and the visible 'wrapped meal' tag. On X the emoji punctuates food-coded and Mexican-coded tweets. The emoji pairs with 🌯 for the layered tamale-and-burrito pair stack and with 🌮 for the layered tamale-and-taco stack.
longForm.whenNotToUse: Skip 🫔 in any context where the read is burrito. The corn husk wrap implies tamale-coded, not flour wrap. Avoid 🫔 in formal contexts where the food-coded read lands as out-of-place.
longForm.howToReply:
If a friend sends 🫔 on a food-coded message, mirror with another 🫔 or 🌮 to match the energy. The tamale chain reads as solidarity.

If 🫔 lands as the Mexican-coded default, reply with another 🫔 or 🧀. And if you want to send 🫔 yourself, pair it with the moment so the tamale-coded read is clear.

faqs.question: What does 🫔 mean in text?
faqs.answer: 🫔 means tamale-coded reference, visible wrapped-meal energy, or the Mexican-food reaction. The green corn husk wrap with tied ends is the visual cue that the read is tamale-coded.

faqs.question: Is 🫔 flirty?
faqs.answer: Rarely. 🫔 usually reads as food-coded rather than flirty; in a dating thread it can read as 'homemade tamales for two' content.

faqs.question: What does 🫔 mean from a girl?
faqs.answer: From a girl or anyone, 🫔 carries the same tamale-coded read. There is no gendered meaning; the emoji works the same regardless.

faqs.question: What does 🫔 mean on Instagram?
faqs.answer: On Instagram, 🫔 is the default sticker on Mexican-food-coded captions and traditional-meal-coded story overlays.
